assessment: The 3D and 1D lattices are genuine, mutually exclusive source-reported experimental configurations. Both use lattice hold time as the plotted independent variable and trapped atom number as the readout, and the TeX reports exponential-fit lifetimes of 54 ms and 220 ms after excluding observations with t_hold < 75 ms. This does not source-close a benchmark Oracle: the TeX gives neither numerical initial trapped-atom amplitudes nor an upper endpoint/common finite hold-time domain, so absolute N_trapped(t_hold) queries cannot be answered from the two time constants. It also reports no uncertainty for either fitted lifetime and no measurement/error model for arbitrary queries. The configurations differ simultaneously in dimensionality, wavelength, polarization, power, detuning, depth, spatial overlap, and loading sequence, so they may only be represented as bundled branches, not as an isolated causal effect of dimensionality. No normalized survival fraction is directly reported in the frozen TeX. The paper is therefore ineligible for drafting from the present source packet.

issues.detail: The TeX says that fit data with t_hold < 75 ms were excluded, but supplies neither the fit endpoint nor the sampled hold times. This is not a finite common query domain and does not justify extrapolating the fitted law to every t_hold >= 75 ms.

The TeX reports only the decay time constants. It states qualitatively that the branches have different initial lattice atom numbers but gives neither numerical initial amplitude, so N_trapped(t_hold) cannot be decoded for either branch. Replacing it with normalized survival would introduce a readout that the frozen TeX does not directly report.

The source calls 54 ms and 220 ms estimated lifetimes but gives no confidence interval, standard error, covariance, residual model, or raw-count uncertainty for these fits. The source packet therefore cannot support calibrated uncertainty for generated evidence.

The two branches are real configurations, but they jointly change dimensionality, wavelength, polarization, power, detuning, lattice depth, overlap, and loading procedure. The source itself attributes the lifetime difference to depth and resonant-scattering/heating differences. A case must not present this pair as an isolated effect of 3D versus 1D geometry.

review_material.assessment: The source reports trapped atom number versus lattice hold time for 3D and 1D optical lattices, with exponential-decay fits yielding lifetimes of 54 ms and 220 ms, respectively. The hold time is a common control, but the source does not provide a numeric domain for hold time beyond the exclusion of t_hold < 75 ms; no upper bound or full range is given. The initial atom number is not quantified in the text. Therefore, a complete numeric response with a finite common hold-time domain cannot be extracted, so case_authoring_ready is false.

anchors.support: To make the 3D (1D) optical lattices, we use a single circularly- (linearly-) polarised laser beam, normally incident near the centre of the grating with wavelength ≈780 nm (1070 nm), power 0.9 W (10 W), and e^-2 intensity radius 2.5 mm (80 μm). For the near-resonant lattice at ≈780 nm, the laser red-detuning was 78 GHz relative to the center of the four Doppler-broadened D2 transitions. Due to the grating period d=1080 nm, the 780 nm light diffracts (±1-order) at an angle of θ=45° to the grating normal with diffraction efficiencies into the first and zeroth orders of η_±1≈35% and η_0≈5% respectively.

fixed_conditions.statement: 3D lattice: single circularly-polarised laser beam, wavelength ~780 nm, power 0.9 W, e^-2 intensity radius 2.5 mm, red detuning 78 GHz from Rb D2 line, grating period 1080 nm, first-order diffraction angle 45 degrees, diffraction efficiencies eta_±1 ~35% and eta_0 ~5%.

anchors.support: To make the 3D (1D) optical lattices, we use a single circularly- (linearly-) polarised laser beam, normally incident near the centre of the grating with wavelength ≈780 nm (1070 nm), power 0.9 W (10 W), and e^-2 intensity radius 2.5 mm (80 μm). The 1070 nm light has most power in the zeroth order η_0≈70%.

fixed_conditions.statement: 1D lattice: single linearly-polarised laser beam, wavelength ~1070 nm, power 10 W, e^-2 intensity radius 80 μm, far-off resonance, grating period 1080 nm, zeroth-order efficiency ~70%.

anchors.support: As a basis for loading the optical lattices, ≈8×10^6 87Rb atoms are loaded into a GMOT and cooled to ≈3 μK using a standard red molasses cooling stage. Stray DC magnetic fields are cancelled by three pairs of orthogonal Helmholtz coils.
The grating chip is bonded to the open end facet of a rectangular cuvette vacuum cell using UHV compatible epoxy, allowing a base vacuum pressure at the 10^-8 mbar level.
For both the 3D and 1D lattice geometries 150 μs long resonant fluorescent images are taken with the MOT light after a 1 ms time of flight following the extinction of the lattice beam.

fixed_conditions.statement: Base vacuum pressure at 10^-8 mbar level; atoms loaded from GMOT with ~8e6 87Rb atoms cooled to ~3 μK; stray DC magnetic fields cancelled by three pairs of orthogonal Helmholtz coils; fluorescence imaging with 150 μs resonant images after 1 ms time of flight following extinction of lattice beam.

anchors.support: A log plot of the number of trapped atoms as a function of hold time in both the 3D and 1D lattice is shown. Exponential decays are fitted, excluding data where t_hold < 75 ms.
Fitted exponential decays reveal estimated lattice lifetimes of 54 ms for the 3D lattice.
From the time constant of the fits we estimate a 3D lattice lifetime of 54 ms.
